This experiment keeps one warp on adjacent X outputs at fixed Y/Z but uses a (32,16) block, reducing the grid from 1024 to 512 CTAs relative to (32,8). It tests whether fewer, larger CTAs help this small workload or instead increase resource pressure; no speedup is assumed.

This experiment tests a contrasting (32,4) CTA shape—still one adjacent-X row per warp, but splitting each X row across two CTAs—and explicit if/else single-step boundary correction instead of the earlier predicate-style correction. Its larger CTA count could hurt a tiny workload; no speedup is assumed.
